# v2.0.0 — Security hardening, first-run setup and notification preferences

This major release fixes four privately reported security vulnerabilities and
hardens accounts, events and public RSVPs. It replaces the `HOST_INVITE_CODE`
variable with a first-administrator setup page, and adds recipient notification
preferences, paired sign-in codes, configurable event URLs, offline background
effects and occasion presets. RSVP to Me is now licensed under AGPL-3.0-only.

Startup applies twelve database migrations and converts saved provider
credentials to a new encryption format. **The upgrade is one-way:** the only
supported way back to v1.5.0 is restoring the backup taken before upgrading. Read
the breaking-change checklist in the
[upgrade guide](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md#breaking-change-checklist)
before you start.

## Changes

### Security

- Fix four vulnerabilities reported privately (#872):
  - [GHSA-wx7r-qqc6-2v5v](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/security/advisories/GHSA-wx7r-qqc6-2v5v)
    (high): sessions stayed valid after account deletion. Sessions are now
    checked in PostgreSQL on every request.
  - [GHSA-mrf6-4xh5-7p47](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/security/advisories/GHSA-mrf6-4xh5-7p47)
    (high): missing ownership and access checks across events.
  - [GHSA-wch3-85cq-qp5f](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/security/advisories/GHSA-wch3-85cq-qp5f)
    (medium): host and profile input was stored without validation.
  - [GHSA-8r3w-c2hj-fv38](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/security/advisories/GHSA-8r3w-c2hj-fv38)
    (medium): registration and emailed-link hardening. Registration changes
    require sign-in proof, co-host invitations require explicit acceptance,
    and sign-out is a same-origin POST.
- Require guests who give an email address or phone number on a public RSVP to
  verify it with a code before the RSVP is saved. (#792, #895)
- Encrypt saved SMTP, Cloudflare and Twilio credentials with versioned keys and
  random salts, converted automatically at startup after a mandatory backup.
  (#328, #339, #788)
- Apply per-IP rate limits only when `TRUSTED_IP_HEADER` names a trusted proxy
  header, so unrelated guests no longer share one site-wide limit. (#847, #873)
- Enforce RSVP rules on the server. (#848, #874)
- Validate the Cloudflare account ID before building API URLs. (#916, #922)
- Complete input validation and backup safeguards, and stop caching dynamic
  downloads. (#778, #851, #871)

### New features

- Set up the first administrator at `/setup`, by verifying a sign-in sent to
  `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL`. Invite codes are managed in the Admin Panel, and normal
  installations no longer need baseline seeding. (#877, #882)
- Sign in with a six-digit code as well as the emailed or texted link. (#844,
  #862)
- Recipient notification preferences: each person chooses which kinds of
  messages they receive, per event, by email, SMS or both, after verifying each
  address. Event updates and manual host messages honor these choices. (#335,
  #789, #790, #800, #896)
- Edit or regenerate event URLs. New Unlisted and Private events get random
  six-character URLs. (#880, #884)
- Remove an event password from **Display options**, with confirmation. (#878,
  #883)
- Background effects work offline: mix up to three icons from a bundled Noto
  Emoji library, searchable in English, Dutch, German and Spanish, and set their
  amount, size, speed and movement. (#825, #827, #828)
- Occasion theme presets with editable default effects. (#836)
- One **Guest RSVP display** table for Going, Maybe, Can't make it and a new
  Invited row; counts can be shown even when names are hidden. (#811, #826)
- A 100 MiB upload quota per account, with automatic cleanup of images nothing
  uses. (#850, #876)

### Accessibility and design

- Every button, field, switch and message uses one theme-aware control set, and
  event themes and emails derive readable text and link colors. (#807, #808,
  #809, #815, #817, #823)
- The app chrome and app pages follow the design language. (#812, #855)
- Host controls are named, filters are labeled, and confirmations share one
  dialog. Every page has a main landmark and a skip link, and RSVP fields have
  visible labels with announced, linked errors. (#795, #810, #824, #853, #881)
- Event cards and pages show times in the event's own timezone. (#853, #881)

### Fixes

- Harden reminder and delivery reliability. The optional Cloudflare email worker
  no longer acknowledges automated or bulk mail. (#849, #875)
- Fix feed, admin, upload and moderation issues found in QC. (#850, #876)
- Administrators moderating an event keep access to its settings and guest
  list. (#859)
- The floating RSVP card no longer oscillates at its docking line. (#804)
- Complete the Dutch translation; every language must now be complete. (#793,
  #801, #914, #923)

### Maintenance

- License RSVP to Me under AGPL-3.0-only, and add a contribution guide and issue
  forms. (#796, #797, #798)
- Update Next.js to 16.4.6, iron-session to 9.1.0, Nodemailer to 10.6.0,
  next-intl to 4.15.1, the Redis client to 6.3.1, dotenv to 18.0.10 and
  lucide-react to 1.74.0. Development tooling moves to ESLint 10.15.0, Vitest
  5.1.0 and Playwright 1.65.1.
- Patch the transitive effect (GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw) and minimatch
  (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249) advisories. (#902, #915, #921)
- Update the optional email worker's Wrangler toolchain.
- Rehearse the upgrade from the previous release, and every rollback path, in
  Container QC before each release. (#918, #925)

### Looking ahead

Apprise notifications are planned for v3 (#767), and how SMS is configured may
change then. v2.0.0 continues to send SMS through Twilio.

## Upgrade from v1.5.0

1. Work through the
   [breaking-change checklist](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md#breaking-change-checklist).
2. Record the running image digest, `pg_dump` the database, copy `data/uploads`
   and back up `.env`. Keep `.env` unchanged, with the same `SESSION_SECRET` and
   `ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
3. Remove `HOST_INVITE_CODE`. Set `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL`, and make sure email
   delivery works (and SMS, if guests give phone numbers): public RSVPs with a
   contact now need a verification code. Behind a trusted reverse proxy, set
   `TRUSTED_IP_HEADER`.
4. Stop every old app instance. In your deployment Compose file, pin the app
   image to `ghcr.io/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me:2.0.0` after the Release workflow has
   published it. With the standard production configuration, run:

   ```bash
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml pull app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d --no-deps app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml logs --tail=100 app
   ```

5. The first start writes `data/backups/pre-migration/pre-migration-schema_*.sql`,
   applies twelve migrations and converts saved credentials. The log reports
   `[config-secrets] migrate: ... v2 ready.` when the conversion finishes.
6. Check health, sign-in by link and by code, a public RSVP with contact
   verification, a password-protected RSVP, editing with an existing edit link,
   uploads, notification preferences, and delivery through each enabled email
   and SMS provider.
7. If you use the optional Cloudflare email worker, redeploy it (or replace the
   copied **Admin → Email** template) to enable its auto-reply guards.

Hosts will notice that visitors re-enter event passwords once, guests confirm
their email or phone with a code, and new Unlisted and Private events get random
URLs. Existing event links and RSVP edit links keep working.

## Rollback and known limitations

Rolling back by changing only the image is **not** safe. v1.5.0 starts and
reports healthy, but email and SMS sign-in fail because it cannot read the
converted credentials. It also matches poll votes by display name, so one
same-name guest retracting a vote deletes the other's. Running
`db:secrets --rollback` first fixes the credentials but not the votes.

To roll back, stop the app, restore your pre-upgrade `pg_dump` (or the first
`pre-migration-schema_*.sql` that v2.0.0 wrote) into a fresh database with
`psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, and start the v1.5.0 image by its recorded digest
with the same `.env`. No credential downgrade is needed. Everything received
after the upgrade is lost. The
[rollback guide](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md#rolling-back-v200-to-v150)
has the commands.

Builds still download the remaining Google fonts through Next.js and can
encounter the tracked upstream font-query failure. Fonts are served locally at
runtime. Provider tests use mocks; passing CI does not confirm delivery through
your live email or SMS account.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md)
for backup, verification, and release approval procedures.

**Full comparison:** https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/compare/v1.5.0...v2.0.0
